Here, we investigate how the intrinsic thermal asymmetry of a single Janus plasmonic nanoheater is transformed when moving from isolated particles to planar random arrays under continuous-wave illumination. Using coupled electromagnetic and steady-state heat-transfer simulations, we first quantify the finite spatial range over which the single-particle Janus signature remains detectable. We show that neighboring nanoheaters introduce two competing effects: a nearly symmetric collective thermal background that screens and homogenizes the Janus factor, and short-range neighbor-induced asymmetries that partially compensate this screening when interparticle distances become comparable to the spatial extent of the single-particle thermal anisotropy. We derive a closed-form analytical model for the array-averaged Janus factor as a function of nanoparticle number and surface density. The model predicts the screening-dominated regime from single-particle quantities and identifies deviations associated with near-field neighbor-induced contributions at higher densities. These results demonstrate a central trade-off for biomedical photothermal applications in continuous-wave operation: collective heating is required to reach relevant temperature increments, but it progressively erases the directional Janus character by thermal homogenization. Our framework provides a practical route to predict and rationally design the spatial temperature distribution in plasmonic assemblies of Janus particles.

items.title_en: Quantized six-vertex realizations of frustration graphs
items.title_zh: 阻挫图的量子化六顶点实现
items.abstract_en: A recent graph-theoretic criterion for a Hamiltonian to exhibit a free-parafermion spectrum is that its frustration graph be an indifference graph. We show that an arbitrary finite indifference graph can be realized as a frustration graph of the quantized six-vertex model at odd roots of unity, by a suitable choice of the defining wiring diagram and parameters. This provides a concrete realization of the criterion through the quantum Frobenius property of the quantized six-vertex model, recently established from its three-dimensional integrable structure.

items.title_en: Exact analytical spectra of an effective field-modified radial Schrödinger equation by the Nikiforov--Uvarov method
items.abstract_en: We revisit the effective radial Schrödinger equation for a charged spinless particle in collinear static electric and magnetic fields that was formulated in our earlier work within the tridiagonal representation approach (TRA). In that model the angular factor of the electric coupling is replaced by the orientation parameter $C=\cosθ$, the linear Zeeman term is diagonal in the azimuthal quantum number, and the effective field-modified central potential takes the form $V(r)=\Vt(r)+qECr$. Here we show that the same equation can be solved exactly without the TRA, by the Nikiforov--Uvarov (NU) method, once the potential component $\Vt(r)$ is prescribed. Three examples are worked out in closed form: a Kratzer-type component, which yields a linear-plus-Coulomb-plus-inverse-square central potential; a pseudoharmonic-type component, which yields a linear-plus-harmonic-plus-inverse-square potential; and a Hulthén-type component with a repulsive core (Manning--Rosen form), which yields a screened confining potential with a finite number of $s$-wave bound states. For each case we obtain the energy spectrum, the normalized eigenfunctions in terms of Laguerre or Jacobi polynomials, the location of the potential minimum, and closed-form radial moments. The spectra are independent of the orientation $θ$ and of the electric field, in agreement with the structure found by the TRA, while the field enters through the shape of $V(r)$, the radial moments, and the expectation value $\langle V\rangle_k$. All analytical results are confirmed by an independent finite-difference diagonalization.

items.title_en: Pinning of a High-Energy Wavepacket by a Single Impurity
items.abstract_en: We demonstrate that a single repulsive impurity enhances directional confinement of a high-energy wavepacket in a finite two-dimensional lattice of quantum wells. At energies far above the interwell barriers, the impurity suppresses transverse dynamical tunneling while preserving propagation along a principal lattice axis, even as the corresponding classical regular region shrinks. Confinement is strongest at impurity amplitudes comparable to the barrier height and weakens for stronger perturbations. Spectral analysis links this nonmonotonic pinning to the wavepacket's overlap with eigenstates concentrated along the launch direction, consistent with impurity-induced variational scarring. These results show that a single local defect can control quantum propagation over distances far exceeding its own spatial extent.

items.title_en: Directional effects of the Unruh effect on steering harvesting
items.abstract_en: We investigate directional quantum steering harvesting by two uniformly accelerated non-identical Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We show that the Unruh effect does not simply degrade harvested steering, but can reshape its directionality in a strongly parameter-dependent manner. At low detector energy scales, acceleration predominantly suppresses steering, whereas at higher energy scales, moderate acceleration can enhance steering and even activate an initially absent steering direction. Most strikingly, within a finite acceleration window, the Unruh effect enhances steering in one direction while simultaneously suppressing it in the opposite direction, revealing an intrinsically directional influence of relativistic acceleration. Detector non-identicality provides an additional control mechanism: a moderate energy-gap mismatch can enhance or activate one steering direction while suppressing the reverse one, whereas sufficiently large energy-gap mismatch suppresses the harvested steering. Moreover, the maximal steering asymmetry approximately marks the transition from two-way to one-way steering. Our results establish relativistic acceleration and detector non-identicality as means of controlling the strength and directionality of vacuum-harvested quantum correlations.

items.title_en: Loss-Tolerant Measurement-Device-Independent QKD over Untrusted Repeaters via High-Dimensional Time-Bin Multiplexing
items.abstract_en: We propose a loss-tolerant measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) protocol using time-bin-multiplexed single photons entangled with local qubits stored in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers. In each round, Alice and Bob each send a single multiplexed photon to an untrusted intermediary, Charlie. Each photon first becomes entangled with Charlie's NV-center qubits; Charlie then performs entanglement swapping between his NV qubits to establish EPR pairs between Alice's and Bob's local qubits. With $d$ time bins per photon, $\log_2 d + 1$ EPR pairs can be generated per transmitted photon, substantially increasing the probability of EPR-pair creation under limited channel bandwidth. To further mitigate the effects of prolonged memory storage, the protocol employs a memory-insensitive (MI) architecture, where multiple banks of qubits and multiplexed photon routing reduce the effective memory lifetime requirements. This approach enhances loss tolerance, enabling higher secret key rates and secure key distribution over longer distances compared to conventional single-photon protocols. Using the Lo-Chau EPR-QKD framework and Shor-Preskill reduction, we prove that the protocol is secure without trusting intermediate nodes, making it suitable for quantum networks with untrusted repeaters.

items.title_en: A low-cost compact muon detector for millikelvin operation
items.abstract_en: Ionizing radiation produces correlated errors in superconducting qubits, posing some challenges to quantum error correction. In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Cosmic muons are a component of this background that can only be partly shielded against at ground level, but can be tagged by an independent detector inside the cryostat, so that the affected data can be vetoed, or the muon tags incorporated into error correction. We present a low-cost, compact muon detector consisting of two plastic scintillator modules, each read out by a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), operated in coincidence. We characterize the SiPMs from room temperature down to 10 mK, including the breakdown and upper-limit voltages that define the operating bias range. Operated as a muon counter, the detector measures a coincidence rate that, as expected, is independent of temperature within uncertainties and agrees with analytical and Monte Carlo predictions. Below approximately 8 K, each muon event produces two pulses, one narrow and one broad, an effect that, to our knowledge, has not been reported before. Coincidences with an independent muon detector outside the cryostat confirm that muons are still counted reliably in this regime. By studying the appearance of double pulses as a function of temperature and magnetic field up to 4.5 T, we find a behavior consistent with the phase diagram of a type-II superconductor. This links the double pulses to a superconducting material in the SiPM, likely an adhesion layer or diffusion barrier introduced during manufacturing. The mechanism by which the superconducting state produces the second pulse is not yet understood.

items.title_en: Near-field contributions to cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer
items.abstract_en: Embedding materials in optical cavities has emerged as a powerful strategy for controlling their physical properties. In this context, increasing attention has been devoted to the thermal Purcell effect, which describes how the radiative heat transfer between a material and its photonic environ- ment can be modified by the electromagnetic boundary conditions imposed by the cavity. Here, we investigate near-field effects in cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer in planar cavities composed of realistic, dissipative gold mirrors, extending previous work that considered ideal mirrors. We iden- tify the conditions under which near-field effects lead to a substantial enhancement of heat transfer between the material and a photonic thermal bath relative to free space, owing to the strong modi- fication of the photonic local density of states by evanescent modes within the cavity. In particular, we find that radiative heat flow can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude in cavities ranging from nanometer to micrometer scales, depending on the absorber frequency and dipole orientation. These findings suggest that near-field effects may be relevant to polariton chemistry experiments and other systems operating within this cavity length-scale regime. Our results add to the idea that cavities can modify material properties not only by engineering vacuum fluctuations in the strong light-matter coupling regime, but also by controlling radiative dissipation and heat transfer.

items.title_en: Polaritonic self-hybridized critical coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
items.abstract_en: Maximizing the absorption of exciton-polaritons in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) under critical coupling conditions is crucial for developing high-efficiency polariton-based photodetectors, solar cells, and perfect absorbers. Here, we propose a polaritonic critical self-hybridized coupling between Brillouin zone folding driven quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBIC) mode and A excitons in a bulk WS2 metasurface. This polaritonic critical coupling shows robust behavior with respect to the asymmetric parameters of the involved BZF-QBIC mode, in contrast to the asymmetry-sensitive conventional QBIC-based critical coupling. By changing the height of WS2 metasurfaces, we observe a typical anti-crossing behavior with a Rabi splitting of 246.5 meV. Moreover, the maximum absorption value of 0.5 for exciton-polaritons is achieved at the polaritonic critical coupling condition. The large population of excitons provided by bulk WS2 is essential for achieving polaritonic critical coupling and can further enhance polaritonic absorption. This work enables the realization of robust, high-absorption self-hybridized polaritonic critical coupling in TMDCs, and further expedite their applications in high-absorption low-dimensional polaritonic devices.

items.title_en: Strong subadditivity of topological entropy on the torus: Rényi order and non-Abelian structure
items.abstract_en: We classify strong subadditivity for the canonical topological Rényi functional at finite positive orders on an unpunctured torus in the topological quantum field theory of any finite unitary modular tensor category. Universal validity means validity for all pure ground states and all regular region pairs with transverse or disjoint boundaries and compatible corner rounding. At von Neumann order one, the inequality holds universally. For each fixed order strictly between zero and one, universal validity is equivalent to pointedness, meaning that every simple anyon type has quantum dimension one. For every nonpointed category and each finite positive order other than one, we construct a violating pure state and an allowed pair. For a fixed pointed category and fixed order above one, universal validity is equivalent to a same-order modular Fourier entropy bound for every pure state. Global homological constraints on actual unions and intersections and established weighted modular uncertainty prove the order-one theorem. For parallel annuli at fixed flux distribution, the order-one functional is affine in their positive count. At other orders, unequal quantum dimensions on the occupied support induce strict curvature that suitable overlapping regions convert into negative deficits. Under the boundary-charge cutting prescription, the von Neumann theorem extends to arbitrary logical density matrices in the same ground space.

items.title_en: Sorption Molecular Dynamics of Point Defects in 2D Materials with a Machine Learning Potential
items.title_zh: 基于机器学习势的二维材料点缺陷吸附分子动力学
items.abstract_en: Defect engineering is a crucial tool for tuning and tailoring the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials. A key challenge is identifying which defects are kinetically stable at room temperature and sufficiently promising to warrant further investigation. However, identifying stable defects with suitable properties using first-principles calculations, such as density functional theory (DFT) is computationally demanding, effectively limiting the scope of high-throughput studies. In this work, we investigate whether the machine learning interatomic potential MACE can reproduce sorption trends (adsorption vs. absorption) previously obtained from high-throughput DFT calculations and extend the analysis to elevated temperatures. A total of 17,624 defect structures from the ADAQ database are simulated using MACE-accelerated molecular dynamics (MD) at both 0 K and 300 K. The results show that MACE successfully reproduces the overall sorption trends observed in DFT calculations at 0 K at a fraction of the computational cost. Simulations performed at 300 K further indicate that the qualitative sorption trends remain largely the same when including finite-temperature effects. These findings demonstrate that MACE-driven MD can be used as an effective high-throughput prescreening tool for defect-related studies in 2D materials, specially related to sorption. While conventional first-principles methods, such as DFT, remain necessary for accurate and quantitative validation, the use of MLIPs enables MD simulations of finite-temperature defect behavior at a fraction of the computational cost of DFT-based MD.

items.title_en: Dicke model of open-shell atoms with tensor polarizability
items.abstract_en: We study the extended Dicke model obtained from the scalar--vector--tensor polarizability of open-shell atoms coupled to a shared cavity mode. For a single electric-dipole channel, rotational symmetry fixes the tensor to vector ratio; we use $^{168}\mathrm{Er}$ with $J=6$ as a product-state example. A circular pump produces a chiral Raman vertex whose tensor-dependent matrix elements select the occupied Zeeman sector. The resulting first-order transition occurs before the empty-cavity branch loses local stability, and the ordered state is read out through $\langle\hat J_z\rangle$. A linear pump instead produces an empty-cavity $\pm x$ cat and a continuous transition into an even-$m$ cat-like state with order parameter $\langle\hat J_z^2\rangle$. With cavity loss alone, the circular trajectory emits a photon burst and approaches a Raman-dark Zeeman pole rather than a finite-field condensate. In the linear geometry, cavity-bright modes are damped toward the cat-like branch while a dark spin mode remains undamped. These are phenomena of that model; the vector-only controls show that they depend on the channel-fixed tensor coupling.

items.title_en: Advances in quantum optomechanical control based on cavity cold-atom systems
items.abstract_en: Cavity optomechanics represents a frontier research direction in quantum science and technology, centered on the control and exploration of interactions between electromagnetic fields and mechanical motion. Rooted in quantum mechanics, this field realizes efficient coupling and precise manipulation of optical fields and mechanical vibrations through the structural design and precise regulation of optical microcavities and mechanical oscillators, thereby revealing and harnessing novel quantum phenomena. In recent years, cavity optomechanics has evolved into an interdisciplinary frontier integrating quantum optics, condensed matter physics, and quantum precision measurement, exhibiting profound application in both fundamental physics research and quantum information science. With advancements in technologies such as nanomanufacturing and laser cooling, optomechanical interactions have been successfully demonstrated in various experimental systems. Among these platforms, cavity cold-atom systems stand out as one of the ideal platforms for implementing quantum optomechanics. Featuring exceptional environmental isolation, long quantum coherence times, and strong light-matter interaction, these systems provide a crucial testbed for exploring strong and even ultrastrong optomechanical coupling effects as well as rich nonlinear quantum phenomena. This paper reviews the recent progress in optomechanical control and manipulation based on cavity cold-atom systems. We first outline the fundamental principles of standard cavity optomechanical systems. Then, we describe the experimental realization of linear and nonlinear optomechanical couplings in cold-atom systems. After that, we focus on the representative applications of this platform in high-precision quantum sensing, quantum memory, and the preparation of macroscopic nonclassical states. Finally, we give an outlook and challenges in this field.

items.title_en: Bias-Modulated Electronically-Tunable Optoelectronic Chromatic Dispersion in Ge PN Photodiodes
items.title_zh: Ge PN 光电二极管中偏压调制的电可调谐光电色散
items.abstract_en: Optoelectronic Chromatic Dispersion (OED) is a source of significant wavelength-dependent current in photodiodes, offering a pathway to computational spectroscopy in a photodiode-only platform without the need for additional optical or mechanical components. Previous studies have activated OED through light modulation. Here, we present a theoretical and experimental investigation of bias-modulated OED in the C- and L-bands in a Ge PN photodiode, where the applied bias voltage is modulated sinusoidally, and the optical illumination is held constant. The spectral response is due to wavelength-dependent optical absorption together with bias-dependent competition between carrier drift, displacement current, and mobile-charge screening. With the RF phase-shift technique, the maximum measured OED sensitivity is +4.13 deg/nm in the L-band, significantly larger than that of light-modulated OED in Ge. The 15 mdeg phase-noise floor yields a spectral resolution of 3.6 pm. These results establish bm-OED as an electronically reconfigurable dispersive mechanism for applications in chip-scale computational spectrometers, photonic integrated circuits (PICs), on-chip RF photonics, and wavelength-division multiplexing.

items.title_en: Metric-Changing Quasi-Hermitian Quenches: Normalized Loschmidt Amplitude and Complex-Time Zeros
items.abstract_en: In quasi-Hermitian mixed-state quenches, the initial and final Hamiltonians generally possess different positive-definite metrics, so post-quench evolution is not quasi-unitary in the initial physical space. Choosing the preparation/measurement space as reference, we derive from first principles a normalized mixed-state Loschmidt amplitude using metric-compatible purifications. The resulting biorthogonal trace representation contains a normalization factor given by the norm of the evolved purification in the initial metric; this factor is essential for comparing states from different physical Hilbert spaces and directly encodes the metric mismatch. We prove that this normalization function is strictly positive on the real-time axis, so real-time criticality arises solely from destructive interference in the dynamical overlap. In complex time, zeros of the normalization factor generate branch singularities distinct from Fisher zeros. For a general two-level system, we derive analytic expressions for the Fisher and normalization zeros and analyze exceptional-point scaling together with the temperature- and quasi-Hermiticity-dependent DQPT critical times in two solvable quench protocols. In contrast to metric-stationary quenches, where non-Hermitian effects may be absorbed into an equivalent Hermitian description, the metric mismatch here produces genuine non-Hermitian dynamics: a time-dependent normalization factor and complex-time branch structure that cannot be removed by any global similarity transformation.

items.title_en: Multi-Instantons and Exact-WKB Stokes Jumps in Multi-Well Quantum Mechanics
items.abstract_en: We study the relation between the exact-WKB Delabaere--Dillinger--Pham Stokes jumps and the multi-instanton expansion of a one-dimensional potential with $N$ equal-depth minima. For a single barrier this relation is the Bogomolny--Zinn-Justin cancellation between the instanton--anti-instanton ambiguity and the Borel ambiguity of perturbation theory, and we extend it to every consecutive barrier interval and to the integration contours themselves. In the dilute large-$T$ regime at fixed nonperturbative grade, we derive the quasi-zero mode integral over the instanton separations from the Euclidean path integral and reduce it to Gamma and Hankel periods. With the local Weber level function of each well and one normalization per well fixed by the local Weber connection matrix, these periods reproduce the two lateral connected exact-WKB coefficients. The two lateral contours of each instanton--anti-instanton separation differ by exactly one Hankel cycle, and this linear Picard--Lefschetz relation reproduces the Stokes jump of the connected coefficient. A numerical solution of the Schrödinger equation for a symmetric triple well confirms the resulting two-barrier level splitting. At higher fixed grade, the map from ordered event sequences to normalized scalar coefficient products is not one-to-one. At leading dilute order the scalar weight of a closed event sequence depends only on the numbers of barrier crossings, $\mathcal I\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs, and $\mathcal I\mathcal I$/$\bar{\mathcal I}\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs. We construct two inequivalent grade-six triple-well event sequences with the same product of local Weber amplitudes, which embed in every potential with $N\ge3$ wells. Our results hold within the regular dilute, one-loop, local Weber approximation.

items.title_en: Hyperentanglement in intermediate phase-space planes: benchmarking a photon-pair source for quantum key distribution
items.abstract_en: We characterize a source of photon pairs simultaneously entangled in polarization and in the transverse spatial degree of freedom, with the spatial measurements performed in intermediate planes of the fractional Fourier transform. The source consists of two crossed type-I crystals in a non-collinear geometry, such that the transverse variables carry information about the crystal of origin. Detection in the crystal plane reveals this information completely and destroys the polarization entanglement, so that a scheme using the near and far fields as conjugate spatial bases cannot support a parallel polarization channel. In intermediate planes both spatial bases combine position and momentum, such that the which-crystal information is partially erased, and the polarization entanglement survives in all four combinations of spatial bases. Applying Bell and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen criteria to the same photon pairs certifies both degrees of freedom simultaneously. We evaluate quantum bit error rates and asymptotic secret key rates in each degree of freedom, and find that the source delivers two simultaneously usable channels per photon pair.

items.title_en: Inferring Transition-Dipoles from Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy with Deep Learning
items.title_zh: 利用深度学习从二维红外光谱推断跃迁偶极矩
items.abstract_en: Two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy is a powerful nonlinear technique for probing vibrational couplings, anharmonicities, coherence, and molecular dynamics. Among the microscopic parameters encoded in 2D IR spectra, transition dipoles are fundamental quantities that characterize molecular structure and govern light-matter interactions. However, reconstructing these quantities from spectroscopic data remains a challenging inverse problem. Here, we introduce a physics-informed convolutional neural network (CNN), Spec2DipoleNet, trained on 2D IR spectra generated via the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian (NHH) method. This multi-task CNN reconstructs the transition dipole matrices under physically-motivated masking constraints. On the validation set, the model achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.085, an $R^2$ of 0.97, and a normalized cross-correlation of 0.98. It reliably recovers matrix elements associated with allowed transitions, while larger deviations are observed for nominally forbidden transitions. Our results suggest that transition dipole operators can be quantitatively inferred from 2D IR spectra, highlighting the potential of physics-informed deep learning for extracting microscopic quantum parameters from multidimensional spectroscopic data.

items.title_en: Preservation of photon statistics upon selective molecular modulation in hollow-core fibers
items.abstract_en: Preserving the underlying statistical properties of light during frequency transduction is essential for interfacing spectrally disparate quantum systems. To do this successfully, the process needs to be highly efficient, broadband and noiseless. Despite significant progress in this field, satisfying all these conditions remains challenging. Recently, molecular modulation-based transduction in hollow-core fibers has emerged as a promising approach, where biphoton correlations were proven to be preserved during frequency up-conversion. However, beyond this previous demonstration of correlation-maintaining conversion, whether molecular modulation can preserve more general statistical properties of light remains experimentally unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the conservation of photon-number statistics during selective frequency transduction by Raman molecular modulation in a hydrogen-filled hollow-core fiber. As a proof of concept, weak 585-nm signals are selectively converted to 773 nm in the near-infrared and to 471 nm in the blue spectral region with near-unity efficiencies. Phase matching between the generated coherence waves and the transitions of interest is achieved through the effective dispersion of the system, enabling independent selection of the frequency up- and down-conversion processes. The preservation of the photon-number statistics of the shifted signals, along with the large frequency shifts, broad tunability and compatibility with quantum-optical fields, provides a versatile fiber-based platform for quantum frequency transduction. In particular, the demonstrated interfacing between visible and near-infrared wavelengths using low pump energies and low gas pressures offers a route towards connecting spectrally distinct quantum systems, including quantum emitters, sensors and atomic quantum memories, within hybrid quantum networks.

items.title_en: Testing graph isomorphism using simple quantum circuits
items.abstract_en: The graph isomorphism problem asks whether two graphs are equivalent up to a permutation of their vertices. Its precise computational complexity remains unresolved, and it is still unknown whether a polynomial-time algorithm exists. We investigate whether simple graph-dependent Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-time (IQP) and Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) circuits can distinguish non-isomorphic graphs. We first show that suitable IQP and QAOA constructions allow the underlying graph to be reconstructed using a polynomial number of samples. Building on previous work using the QAOA energy, we show that Hamming weight distributions can distinguish graph pairs at circuit depths for which the numerically computed energy gap is zero. We then apply graph invariants to the matrix of ZZ correlators on the output distribution. For the specific case of the graph spectrum, at QAOA depth $p=2$, this invariant numerically distinguishes all $10{,}486$ cospectral regular graph pairs tested on up to 18 vertices. For IQP circuits, we introduce a finer invariant based on probability multiplicities within Hamming weight sectors, which distinguishes every non-isomorphic graph pair tested numerically. Finally, we derive exact graph-theoretic characterisations of the IQP output distribution at $θ=π/2$ and $θ=π/4$. These results show that simple graph-dependent quantum circuits encode substantial structural information, while leaving open whether this information can be extracted efficiently for general graph isomorphism.

items.title_en: Observation of correlations beyond the single-particle picture in fermionic counting statistics
items.abstract_en: The analysis of charge fluctuations in a mesoscopic device can shed light on the fundamental question of whether or not a single-particle picture of electron transport is appropriate, even in the presence of Coulomb interaction. It has been shown on general grounds that mapping the interacting system onto a fermionic single-particle description is subject to strict constraints on the charge-transfer statistics. These constraints can be formulated in terms of a sign rule for the factorial cumulants of the full counting statistics. We report here on the experimental observation of a sign-rule violation in a most elementary model system, i.e. a single-level quantum dot, and provide theoretical modeling that can quantitatively reproduce the experimental data. This reveals the presence of correlations introduced by electron-electron interaction.

items.title_en: Joint-measurement advantage and finite-time transitions in accelerated detector registers
items.abstract_en: The Unruh response thermalizes accelerated detectors, but the entanglement remaining in a register does not by itself specify what distributed measurements can recover. We study this distinction for a four-qubit cluster state whose two assisting nodes independently undergo generalized amplitude damping, while the target nodes remain isolated and the environments are inaccessible. We derive the exact joint-assisted concurrence and the exact one-way value for arbitrary local measurements. The joint optimum equals the bipartition negativity, and computational-basis measurements attain the one-way optimum. A polar-decomposition argument, together with compactness, establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for separable measurements to attain the joint optimum and proves a strict gap whenever this condition fails. For assisting detectors at equal Unruh temperature with relaxation-rate ratio $r>1$, joint advantage exists precisely when the thermal excitation factor satisfies $q<1/r$. At finite positive temperature it ends at a unique finite time, while the remaining entanglement is nonzero. For $r=2$, both the transition time and remaining resource have closed expressions. These results identify when joint assistance is necessary within the independent weak-coupling thermalization model.

items.title_en: Improved Quantum Algorithms for Rényi Entropies Estimation
items.abstract_en: Entropy estimation of discrete probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistical inference and quantum property estimation. In this paper, we study the problem of estimating Rényi entropy $H_α(\mathbf{p})$ for any distribution $\mathbf{p} = (p_i)_{i=1}^n$ given its purified quantum query-access. For non-integer $α> 1$, our algorithm estimates $H_α(\mathbf{p})$ to within additive error $ε$ using only $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{\max\{1/2,1-1/α\}}/ε\big)$ queries, which improves the best known upper bound for dependence on both $n$ and $1/ε$. For $0<α<1$, our algorithm has query complexity $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{1/(2α)}/ε^{\max\{1,1/(2α)\}}\big)$, which improves the dependence on $1/ε$ of the current best upper bound without incresing its $n$ dependence. Our approach adapts the multi-level estimation framework to relative approximation of the power sums and leverage binary search to remove the requirement of prior knowledge of them. We also strengthen the precision-dependent lower bound to $Ω\big(1/ε^{\max\{1,1/(2α)\}}\big)$ for $0<α<1$, which identifies the optimal precision dependence of our algorithm.

items.title_en: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
items.title_zh: 基于测试时训练的潜在压缩（Latent Compaction）
items.abstract_en: Long contexts enlarge key--value (KV) caches, increasing memory use and attention costs during generation. Compressing these caches must preserve information for unseen questions. We introduce **Latent Compaction**, which learns a compact document-specific cache through test-time training. We initialize cache entries using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity. Training first fits attention outputs and log-normalizers to those of the full cache, with reconstruction-selected entries held fixed. It then jointly optimizes the entire cache through end-to-end distillation from the full-cache model. Model weights remain frozen throughout, and training uses only generic prompts about the document, without access to downstream questions or answers. Experiments on RULER, LongBench, and Phonebook Lookup demonstrate substantial gains over budget-matched compression baselines. On a RULER, for example, our method achieves 96.7% accuracy at 32$\times$ compression, compared with 40.0% for KVZip+. The method also transfers across model scales and families, with retrieval gains on both Qwen3 and MiniCPM5. These results show that treating the KV cache as a neural network and optimizing it with test-time training can preserve retrieval accuracy under aggressive compression. The code is released at https://www.github.com/THUNLP/latent-compaction
items.abstract_zh: 长上下文会放大键值（KV）缓存，增加生成时的内存占用与注意力开销；压缩缓存又必须保留回答未知问题的信息。我们提出 Latent Compaction：通过测试时训练为每个文档学习一个紧凑的缓存。缓存条目依据重构重要性、教师注意力与键空间多样性进行初始化；训练先让注意力输出与对数归一化器拟合完整缓存，并固定重构选中的条目，再通过完整缓存模型的端到端蒸馏联合优化整个缓存。全程冻结模型权重，且只用关于文档的通用提示，无需接触下游问答。在 RULER、LongBench 与 Phonebook Lookup 上，本方法显著优于同预算压缩基线：例如 RULER 上 32× 压缩达 96.7% 准确率，而 KVZip+ 为 40.0%，并可跨模型规模与家族迁移。
items.highlight_zh: 把 KV 缓存当作可训练网络，32× 压缩仍达 96.7% 准确率
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：长上下文会让 Transformer 的 KV 缓存变得很大，拖慢生成并占用显存。已有的缓存压缩方法往往保不住回答“没见过的下游问题”所需的信息。
方法：作者提出 Latent Compaction——把每个文档的 KV 缓存当作一个可训练的小型“神经网络”，在测试时（推理阶段）针对该文档做优化，而模型本身的权重完全冻结。初始化时用三种线索决定保留哪些缓存条目：重构重要性、教师模型的注意力、键空间多样性。训练分两步：先固定重构选中的条目，让注意力输出与对数归一化器去拟合完整缓存；再通过完整缓存模型的端到端蒸馏，联合优化整个缓存。训练全程只用关于文档的通用提示，完全不知道下游问题和答案。
结果：在 RULER、LongBench 和 Phonebook Lookup 上，同等压缩预算下明显优于基线。例如 RULER 上 32 倍压缩仍达 96.7% 准确率，而 KVZip+ 只有 40.0%；方法还能跨模型规模与家族迁移（Qwen3 与 MiniCPM5 的检索指标均有提升）。
为何重要：它表明把 KV 缓存当作可优化对象、用测试时训练来压缩，能在激进压缩下保住检索能力，为长上下文推理降本提供了新思路。

items.title_en: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
items.title_zh: VASPO：带特权价值估计的自蒸馏
items.abstract_en: On-policy self-distillation provides dense supervision for reasoning models via a privileged self-teacher. However, this supervision reflects local token preferences rather than the expected return of an unguided student continuation. Recent methods combine this signal with GRPO. They use GRPO for update directions and the teacher for signal scaling. However, we demonstrate a more effective integration within PPO. Specifically, we identify complementary positional dynamics: privileged information enhances a critic's value-prediction accuracy toward the response's end, whereas self-teacher guidance is strong initially, drops mid-generation, and rebounds finally. These insights motivate Value-Augmented Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (VASPO), wherein a self-teacher and critic evaluate identical privileged information at student-generated prefixes. The critic computes token-level PPO advantages from predicted continuation returns, while the self-teacher modulates selected positive advantages via bounded probability ratios. Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VASPO improves mean accuracy over PPO by 2.59 and 1.81 percentage points on Qwen3-4B and OLMo3-7B variants, respectively, and achieves the highest mean accuracy among evaluated methods on Knights and Knaves. Our code is available at https://github.com/cii030/VASPO.
items.abstract_zh: 在线策略自蒸馏借助特权自教师为推理模型提供密集监督，但这种监督反映的是局部 token 偏好，而非无引导学生续写的期望回报。近期方法将其与 GRPO 结合（GRPO 定更新方向、教师做信号缩放），我们则证明在 PPO 框架内整合更为有效。我们发现二者存在互补的位置动态：特权信息能提升 critic 在回答末尾附近的价值预测精度，而自教师引导在生成初期较强、中段下降、末尾回升。据此提出 VASPO（Value-Augmented Self-Distillation Policy Optimization）：自教师与 critic 在学生生成的前缀上评估相同的特权信息，critic 由预测的续写回报计算 token 级 PPO 优势，自教师则用有界概率比调节选定的正优势。在六个数学推理基准上，VASPO 相比 PPO 在 Qwen3-4B 与 OLMo3-7B 变体上平均准确率分别提升 2.59 与 1.81 个百分点，并在 Knights and Knaves 上取得所评估方法中的最高平均准确率。
items.highlight_zh: 用 PPO 的 critic 承载特权价值估计，六个数学基准平均准确率提升约 2 点
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究问题：让大模型做数学推理时，如何更充分地利用“特权信息”（例如标准答案）来产生更密集、更可靠的训练信号？已有做法是让学生模型同时扮演“自教师”，在每一步给出偏好信号，但这种信号只是局部的 token 偏好，并不等于一段完整回答的真实收益。

2. 方法：作者提出的 VASPO 让 critic 和自教师看同一份特权信息，但分工不同。critic 从预测的续写回报出发，算出 token 级的 PPO 优势，相当于从“整段回答值多少分”这个全局视角评价每一步；自教师则用有界的概率比对选中的正向优势做微调，相当于给出局部引导。作者还发现两者的作用位置互补：critic 在回答末尾更准，自教师信号则在开头强、中段弱、结尾回升，因此把它们放在 PPO 里配合比放进 GRPO 更自然。

3. 结果：在六个数学推理基准上，VASPO 比 PPO 在 Qwen3-4B 上平均准确率高 2.59 个百分点，在 OLMo3-7B 上高 1.81 个百分点，并在 Knights and Knaves 任务上取得所有对比方法中的最高平均准确率。

4. 意义：这项工作说明“特权监督”不一定要当作独立奖励来用，它可以与强化学习本身的价值估计互补，从而更稳定地提升推理能力，为后续自蒸馏与 RL 结合的研究提供了具体的设计思路。

items.title_en: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: Mosaic：多会话智能体强化学习
items.abstract_en: Most existing agentic reinforcement learning methods assume single-session trajectories, where interaction proceeds within one continuously accumulated context. However, agentic techniques such as context compaction and subagent forking may produce trajectories spanning multiple sessions, creating a mismatch between the single-session training assumption and inference-time execution. Therefore, we introduce Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning, a more general setting that supports an arbitrary number of sessions within a trajectory. Under this setting, a widely adopted method is to broadcast trajectory-level advantages to all sessions, but this does not distinguish contributions from various sessions or guide session allocation within trajectories. To address this issue, we propose Mosaic, a multi-session agentic RL method with critic-free hierarchical optimization. At the trajectory level, it incorporates session-usage signals into advantage estimation. At the session level, it shapes each session's advantage according to the estimated marginal contribution. Experiments on BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B show that Mosaic outperforms broadcasting in both context compaction and subagent forking scenarios while using fewer sessions on average. Further analyses show that our method achieves improvements in session utility and allocation, which we suggested is a promising target for future advances in multi-session agentic RL.
items.abstract_zh: 现有大多数智能体强化学习方法假设单会话轨迹，即交互在一个持续累积的上下文中进行。然而上下文压缩（context compaction）与子智能体分叉（subagent forking）等智能体技术可能产生跨越多个会话的轨迹，造成单会话训练假设与推理时执行之间的不匹配。为此我们提出多会话智能体强化学习，一个支持轨迹内任意数量会话的更一般设定。该设定下，一种广泛采用的方法是把轨迹级优势广播到所有会话，但这无法区分各会话的贡献，也无法指导轨迹内的会话分配。我们提出 Mosaic，一种采用无评论家（critic-free）分层优化的多会话智能体 RL 方法：在轨迹层，把会话使用信号纳入优势估计；在会话层，依据估计的边际贡献塑造每个会话的优势。在 BrowseComp 上使用 Qwen3.5-4B 的实验表明，Mosaic 在上下文压缩与子智能体分叉两种场景中都优于广播方法，且平均使用的会话数更少。进一步分析显示，我们的方法在会话效用与会话分配上均有改进，这被认为是多会话智能体 RL 未来进展的一个有前景的方向。
items.highlight_zh: 用分层优势估计区分各会话贡献，优于优势广播且更省会话
items.digest_zh:
• 研究了什么：现有智能体强化学习几乎都假设“单会话轨迹”，即所有交互串在一个不断累积的上下文里完成。但实际部署常用的上下文压缩（context compaction）、子智能体分叉（subagent forking）等技术，会让一条轨迹跨越多个会话，导致训练假设与推理执行不匹配。
• 用了什么方法：作者提出“多会话智能体强化学习”这一更一般的设定，允许一条轨迹里有任意多个会话。常见做法是把轨迹级的优势广播给所有会话，但这样既无法区分各会话的贡献，也无法指导会话分配。为此他们提出 Mosaic：无 critic 的分层优化——轨迹层把会话使用信号并入优势估计，会话层按估计出的边际贡献塑造每个会话的优势。
• 得到什么结果：在 BrowseComp 上以 Qwen3.5-4B 测试，Mosaic 在上下文压缩和子智能体分叉两种场景中都优于广播基线，而且平均消耗的会话数更少。进一步分析显示，会话效用与会话分配两方面都有改善。
• 为何重要：把“会话”当作可优化、可分配的单位，弥补了训练与推理之间的结构性错位，也指出后续多会话智能体 RL 值得深挖的方向。

items.title_en: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
items.title_zh: 你的 Transformer 其实是弹性的
items.abstract_en: Scaling up transformers has produced models with broad capabilities, deployed across heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads. Yet, model families offer only a few fixed sizes (e.g., S, B, L), forcing users to commit to a model based on hardware and latency constraints. This rigidity is often suboptimal under varying query loads. We introduce a retraining-free method that elastifies pre-trained transformers into a single model that adapts on-the-fly across a continuum of computational budgets. Our key contribution is a differentiable relaxation of the functional unit-ranking problem: unlike prior work, which optimizes a single importance weight per MLP block or attention head, we rank every individual MLP neuron and attention head jointly, on a common scale, by minimizing the model's loss under soft pruning across many sparsity targets, all at once. Across 27 vision and text transformer encoders ranging from 22M to 8B parameters, our method yields smooth degradation up to 60% sparsity and outperforms one-shot baselines under deep pruning. For example, pruning DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 to 50% sparsity removes 427M parameters while reducing ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy by only 0.8%, without the need for weight correction or retraining. At 60% sparsity, a pruned AugReg ViT-B/16 model achieves up to $1.80\times$ higher throughput and $1.26\times$ lower single-query latency on an A100 GPU. Elastic models are produced in minutes, with construction time scaling sub-linearly with parameter count.
items.abstract_zh: 扩大 Transformer 规模造就了能力广泛的模型，它们需部署在异构硬件与波动负载之上。但模型家族通常只提供少数固定尺寸（如 S、B、L），用户只能依据硬件与延迟约束选定其一，在查询负载变动时往往并非最优。我们提出一种免重训练方法，将预训练 Transformer 弹性化为单一模型，可在连续的计算预算范围内即时调整。关键贡献是对功能单元排序问题的可微松弛：以往方法为每个 MLP 块或注意力头优化单一重要性权重，我们则把每个 MLP 神经元与注意力头放在同一尺度上联合排序，通过在许多稀疏目标下同时最小化软剪枝后的损失来实现。在 27 个视觉与文本 Transformer 编码器（22M 至 8B 参数）上，该方法在高达 60% 稀疏度下仍平滑退化，并在深度剪枝时优于一次性基线。例如将 DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 剪枝至 50% 稀疏度可移除 4.27 亿参数，ImageNet-1k 线性探测精度仅下降 0.8%，无需权重修正或重训练；60% 稀疏度下，剪枝后的 AugReg ViT-B/16 在 A100 上吞吐最高提升 1.80 倍、单查询延迟降低 1.26 倍。弹性模型的构建只需数分钟，构建时间随参数量次线性增长。
items.highlight_zh: 免重训练让预训练 Transformer 变成任意计算预算可调的弹性模型
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究问题：现在的 Transformer 模型家族往往只给几个固定尺寸（S、B、L），用户部署时得按硬件和延迟挑一个。可实际推理请求的负载是波动的，固定尺寸要么浪费算力，要么拖慢响应，缺乏灵活性。

2. 方法：作者提出一种无需重训练的方法，把一个预训练模型“弹性化”成单个可即时切换计算量的模型。核心技术是把“该保留哪些功能单元”变成一个可微的排序问题：以往工作通常只给每个 MLP 块或注意力头算一个重要性权重，粒度太粗；这里则把每一个 MLP 神经元和每一个注意力头放到同一把尺子上联合排序，做法是同时面向许多个稀疏度目标，最小化软剪枝后的损失。这样一次优化就得到一条完整的“精度—预算”曲线。

3. 结果：在 27 个视觉与文本 Transformer 编码器（22M 到 8B 参数）上验证，稀疏度到 60% 仍平滑退化，深度剪枝时优于一次性剪枝基线。比如把 DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 剪到 50% 稀疏度，删掉 4.27 亿参数，ImageNet-1k 线性探测精度只掉 0.8%，且不需要权重修正或重训练；60% 稀疏度下，剪过的 AugReg ViT-B/16 在 A100 上吞吐最高提升 1.80 倍，单次查询延迟降低 1.26 倍。整个构建过程只要几分钟，耗时随参数量次线性增长。

4. 意义：一个 checkpoint 就能覆盖从大算力到小算力的连续预算，部署时按负载实时切换，省去为每种尺寸单独训练和存储模型的成本，对实际工程部署很有价值。

items.title_en: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
items.title_zh: LIBERO-PeRM：个性化机器人操作基准
items.abstract_en: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.
items.abstract_zh: 个性化是通用机器人进入家庭环境、实现真正实用性的关键。虽然通用机器人操作已被广泛研究，但个性化机器人操作（PeRM）缺乏一个能把任务完成与偏好满足区分开的受控基准。我们提出 LIBERO-PeRM，一个面向具身智能体偏好学习的基准，研究五个问题：1）策略在零样本设定下如何遵循偏好；2）如何从示范中学习单一偏好；3）示范增多时获取偏好的效率如何；4）学到的偏好如何跨布局与任务泛化；5）策略如何组合偏好并在冲突下表现。我们提出仿真中可观测偏好的受控形式化与分类体系，覆盖运动、技能与用户画像选择，并限定为可用语言表达、能在 LIBERO 中不改变任务目标地实例化、可自动评估、可跨任务复用的偏好。基于 LIBERO 的程序化流水线生成成对示范（带与不带偏好）。我们构建五个任务套件（312 个任务），配有高质量示范、丰富元数据与偏好满足度指标。实验表明，当前 VLA 策略在零样本个性化上表现不佳，而 SFT 使偏好变得可学习；混合训练在无偏好保持上优于顺序适配，并在上下文提示下优于仅偏好训练，但可能削弱运动偏好学习；偏好的泛化、分解与冲突处理依然困难。
items.highlight_zh: 首个分离任务完成与偏好满足的个性化机器人操作基准
items.digest_zh:
• 研究了什么：机器人要真正走进家庭，必须学会“个性化”——同样是把杯子拿过来，用户可能偏好用某只手、走某条路径或某种风格。但个性化机器人操作（PeRM）此前缺少一个能把“是否完成任务”与“是否满足偏好”分开衡量的受控基准。
• 用了什么方法：作者提出 LIBERO-PeRM，围绕五个问题设计：策略零样本下能否遵循偏好；能否从示范学会单一偏好；示范增多时学得多快；偏好能否跨布局与任务泛化；多个偏好如何组合、冲突时怎么办。他们把仿真中可观测的偏好做了受控形式化与分类，覆盖运动方式、技能选择与用户画像三类，并限定为可用语言表达、能在 LIBERO 中不改变任务目标地实例化、可自动评估、可跨任务复用的偏好。基于 LIBERO 的程序化流水线生成“带偏好/不带偏好”的成对示范，共五个任务套件、312 个任务。
• 得到什么结果：实验显示当前 VLA 策略零样本个性化表现差；用 SFT 能让偏好变得可学。混合训练在保留无偏好能力上优于顺序适配，在上下文提示下也优于只训练偏好，但可能削弱运动类偏好的学习；偏好泛化、分解与冲突处理依然困难。
• 为何重要：它提供了可自动评测、可复现的个性化操作试验台，让“个性化”这一模糊目标变成可以量化比较的研究问题。

items.title_en: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
items.title_zh: PathFM：多变量轨迹的快速生成式预测
items.abstract_en: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws. Together, these enable PathFM to generate multiple paths for a single series in roughly the time needed for one query to a quantile model. The distilled sampler also makes it practical to optimize a calibration loss directly. PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on the established forecasting benchmarks fev-bench and TIME. To complement these evaluations, we introduce Forecast Path Score Bench (fps-bench), which augments fev-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics. PathFM achieves a higher aggregate path score on fps-bench than all evaluated external baselines. Experiments on chaotic systems further show that our flow model sustains long-run variability, while strong baselines rapidly collapse. PathFM makes generative time series forecasting both competitive and practical, enabling diverse downstream applications.
items.abstract_zh: 时间序列基础模型在通用预测中日益流行，但多数领先模型只预测边缘分位数，未规定未来轨迹的依赖结构——而这正是累积需求、峰值负荷、事件时序等轨迹相关量的关键。为此我们提出 PathFM：一种基于轨迹的预测模型，用 flow matching 生成完整的未来路径，并通过蒸馏到一至两步、共享历史注意力缓存，使生成多条路径的耗时约等于一次分位数模型查询，也让直接优化校准损失变得可行。PathFM 在 fev-bench 与 TIME 上边缘精度具竞争力；我们另提出 fps-bench（加入能量与 variogram 分数及下游指标），PathFM 的聚合路径分数高于所有外部基线。混沌系统实验显示其能维持长期变异性，而强基线迅速坍塌。
items.highlight_zh: 用 flow matching 生成完整轨迹，速度快且路径分数超基线
items.digest_zh:
• 问题：时间序列预测中，多数基础模型只给出每个时间点的边缘分位数（如 90% 分位），却不说明这些点之间如何相互关联。这样一来，像“一周累计需求”“峰值负荷”“事件何时发生”这类依赖整条轨迹的量就无法被刻画。
• 方法：作者提出 PathFM，用 flow matching（流匹配）直接生成完整的未来轨迹，而非逐点分位数。并做两处工程优化：把生成模型蒸馏成 1–2 步采样，并在多次采样间共享历史注意力缓存，使生成多条路径的开销接近一次分位数模型查询；采样变快后还能直接优化校准损失。
• 结果：在 fev-bench 与 TIME 基准上边缘精度具竞争力；作者另建 fps-bench，加入能量分数、变差函数（variogram）分数与下游指标，PathFM 的聚合路径分数高于全部外部基线；在混沌系统上能长期维持变异性，而强基线很快坍缩成过于平滑的预测。
• 意义：让“生成式”预测既准又快，可直接服务需要整条轨迹的下游决策，如库存、电网调度与风控。

items.title_en: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
items.title_zh: 重新思考现代混合专家模型中的路由探索
items.abstract_en: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models have become an important approach for scaling model parameters. Modern MoE architectures increasingly combine two design choices: fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts. The former increases expressiveness by enabling more expert combinations at a fixed activation ratio, and the latter introduces experts that are active for every token. We identify an exploration dilemma between these designs: shared experts can make routing less exploratory by reducing the variability of token representations. This conflicts with the greater need for exploration induced by fine-grained expert segmentation due to the combinatorially enlarged routing space. Consequently, the additional expressiveness offered by fine-grained segmentation may not be fully realized in practice. MirrorMoE is proposed to reconcile this exploration dilemma by shrinking the exploration space through token-adaptive suppression of unnecessary experts. MirrorMoE consistently improves performance across model scales.

items.title_en: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
items.title_zh: MLExpert：迈向自主机器学习工程的通用智能体模型
items.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.

items.title_en: Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving
items.title_zh: 用于形式定理证明的Lean图搜索
items.abstract_en: Retrieving relevant lemmas is crucial for formal theorem proving, enabling provers to build machine-checkable proofs from established mathematical results. Recent retrieval systems match library declarations to a target theorem or its intermediate proof steps, but make limited use of multi-hop dependencies among declarations. These dependencies can reveal supporting lemmas that are not necessarily lexically similar to the target theorem but recur in proofs of related problems. To this end, we propose LeanGraphSearch, a graph-based retrieval method for Lean 4 that constructs a graph from Mathlib's forward dependencies and traverses it to uncover supporting lemmas through multi-hop dependency chains. Specifically, LeanGraphSearch links each declaration to the premises it depends on, uses a graph-based ranking algorithm to propagate relevance from semantically matched declarations to their dependencies, and reranks the expanded candidates against the original query. Across two mathematical retrieval benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves recall by up to 12% over the strongest baseline, LeanSearch v2, on MathlibQR and increases coverage of complete annotated proof routes on MathlibMPR, covering up to 3.7% of extra groups. More importantly, we evaluate whether these retrieval gains translate into improved end-to-end theorem proving by integrating LeanGraphSearch into an iterative proving loop guided by Lean feedback. Across three theorem proving benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves pass rate at {8, 16, 32} reflection turns by as much as 40% compared to vanilla prover and at most 10% compared to LeanSearch v2, showing higher accuracy-cost efficiency. These findings highlight the value of dependency graph search for theorem proving and motivate further research on structure-aware search for proof discovery.

items.title_en: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
items.title_zh: 模型与测量不确定性下动态治疗方案的鲁棒强化学习
items.abstract_en: We develop a robust reinforcement learning (RL) framework for learning adaptive treatment policies that generalize across patients and remain reliable under errors in the measured biomarker and shifts in the disease dynamics. By modeling the patient as a hidden context, we address generalization and robustness in a unified manner through robust contextual Markov decision processes. Applying our framework to adaptive therapy for metastatic prostate cancer in a simulator calibrated to clinical data, we obtain generalizable and robust policies that substantially outperform the existing adaptive therapy method. In particular, we attain robustness with almost no loss of performance when the biomarker is accurate and the disease evolves as anticipated, and find that the resulting policy Pareto-dominates the existing method across a diverse array of scenarios. Our findings suggest that robust RL holds great promise as a principled methodology for learning reliable adaptive treatment policies.
items.abstract_zh: 我们提出一个鲁棒强化学习（RL）框架，用于学习可跨患者泛化、且在生物标志物测量误差与疾病动态漂移下仍保持可靠的自适应治疗策略。通过把患者建模为隐藏上下文，我们以鲁棒上下文马尔可夫决策过程统一处理泛化与鲁棒性。我们将该框架应用于按临床数据校准的模拟器中的转移性前列腺癌自适应治疗，得到的策略可泛化且鲁棒，显著优于现有自适应治疗方法。特别地，当标志物准确、疾病按预期演化时，我们几乎不损失性能即获得鲁棒性；结果还显示所得策略在多种情景下帕累托优于现有方法。这表明鲁棒 RL 有望成为学习可靠自适应治疗策略的原则性方法。
items.highlight_zh: 鲁棒RL学到的前列腺癌治疗策略在多种情景下帕累托优于现有方法
items.digest_zh:
• 问题：自适应治疗方案需要根据患者实时状态调整用药，但现实中生物标志物测量有误差，疾病演化也可能偏离预期。传统强化学习（RL）学到的策略往往对这些不确定性很敏感，换一批患者或测量不准就可能失效。
• 方法：作者把每位患者视为“隐藏上下文”，在鲁棒上下文马尔可夫决策过程框架下，统一处理“跨患者泛化”与“对不确定性鲁棒”两件事，去学习在最坏情形下也不差的治疗策略。
• 结果：在按临床数据校准的转移性前列腺癌模拟器上，新策略显著优于现有自适应治疗方法；当标志物准确、疾病按预期演化时几乎不损失性能；在多种情景下都帕累托优于现有方法，即不会在某些情景下明显变差。
• 意义：说明鲁棒 RL 可以成为设计可靠自适应治疗方案的原则性工具，为临床个性化给药提供了兼顾疗效与稳健性的新思路。

items.title_en: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
items.title_zh: 两次从前：时间序列推理的互补表示
items.abstract_en: Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) enable language-based understanding and reasoning over temporal data, yet a fundamental question remains: what information should their time-series representations preserve, and what variation should they factor out? Existing TSLMs typically expose the language model to a single representation, imposing a fixed inductive bias across downstream tasks. We instead introduce complementary representations as a design principle for time-series reasoning. Our model combines two visual views: line plots preserve absolute measurements and the observed coordinate frame, while normalized delay embeddings factor out positive amplitude rescaling and offsets while exposing temporal structure. Dedicated visual encoders integrate both views into a shared language model through visual tokens and multi-level feature fusion. Evaluation-time interventions verify that the two views exhibit distinct invariance profiles, while single-view ablations show that their combination is particularly beneficial beyond basic perception, with the large gains in prediction and reasoning. Built on Qwen3-VL-8B, our dual-view model improves overall TSRBench accuracy from 44.5% with line plots alone to 53.2%, substantially exceeding the strongest evaluated dedicated TSLM baseline at 36.7%. It further achieves 89.9% accuracy on TSExam and 86.8% numerical accuracy on multivariate ChatTS alignment. Together, these results demonstrate that complementary representations provide an effective design principle for general-purpose TSLMs, enabling models to exploit temporal structure without sacrificing access to the original measurement frame.

items.title_en: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
items.title_zh: 学习引导LLM智能体与多智能体系统
items.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift. In this work, we propose a steering agent that supervises execution on the fly and steers the system back on track when drift occurs. The steering agent observes the execution context, deciding when to intervene with a low-cost fast path and how to intervene with a high-cost slow path. To unlock its steering intelligence, the ability to assess goal drift and generate effective interventions, we jointly train the two paths with reinforcement learning, combining a pairwise ranking objective with group-relative policy optimization (GRPO). Experiments on information-seeking search tasks show that the steering agent provides effective supervision for both single-agent and multi-agent systems, improving their performance and efficiency. The learned steering intelligence generalizes to out-of-domain tasks, transfers to unseen executors, and supports controllable intervention frequency without retraining.

items.title_en: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
items.title_zh: 微调前呈线性、微调后可泛化的知识
items.abstract_en: Not all facts a language model can recall support further learning equally well. We distinguish active facts, which support generalization beyond their own recall, from inert facts, which can be recalled but do not support such generalization in a given task. We study this distinction by constructing new relations from existing ones. Take the relation that maps a place to its continent (Paris -> Europe) and assign each of its answers an arbitrary new label (Europe -> crab, Asia -> zebra). The new relation then maps Paris -> crab. We fine-tune the model on the new relation for a subset of subjects, without telling it the original relation or the relabeling rule, and test whether it assigns the corresponding labels to held-out subjects that share an answer in the original relation. Having learned Paris -> crab, does it answer Munich -> crab? Across eleven language models and 70 relations, how linearly readable the original relation is in pretrained representations strongly predicts this generalization. Within each model, the two correlate across relations at Pearson r = 0.87 to 0.92. This association persists when controlling, separately and jointly, for the number of fine-tuning subjects and answers, the model's accuracy on the original relation, and how often the subjects occur in pretraining text. It is also robust to re-randomizing the label assignment and fine-tuning seed, and to replacing the animal labels with labels from thirteen other semantic categories. When we map a fine-tuned model's wrong label back to the original answer it was assigned to, Munich -> zebra becomes Munich -> Asia. Answers recovered this way are more often among the linear probe's top answers for the subject than among the pretrained model's own. Whether a new relation generalizes depends less on whether its facts can be recalled than on how readily their shared structure can be read out linearly.

items.title_en: Backward Compatibility in Zero-Bit Neural Audio Watermarking
items.title_zh: 零比特神经音频水印中的向后兼容性
items.abstract_en: Neural watermarking systems are typically trained as tightly coupled embedder-detector pairs and implicitly assume static deployment. In real-world deployments, embedders and detectors are frequently updated and selectively decoupled for security and versioning purposes, which can break detection in previously embedded content and, more critically, increase false-positive rates on embedders that a given detector is intentionally not intended to recognize. In this paper the concept of backward compatibility in zero-bit audio watermarking is formalized. A training framework is proposed that pairs a new detector with a sequence of frozen legacy embedders (its legacy chain), using a performance-weighted sampling strategy so that the detector retains accuracy across all earlier versions. This coupling, while necessary for backward compatibility, is shown to induce an embedder-collapse effect that catastrophically degrades the true negative rate (TNR) against out-of-chain embedders. To counteract this, a Angular Diversity Loss (ADL) is introduced that explicitly forces each new embedder to occupy a distinct region of the output space. The combined approach restores near-perfect TNR with no measurable cost to detection accuracy or perceptual audio quality.

items.title_en: Towards Continual Learning: Mitigating Forgetting With Subspace Tuning
items.title_zh: 迈向持续学习：利用子空间调优缓解遗忘
items.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) acquire new skills through fine-tuning, but it can destroy capabilities they already have: catastrophic forgetting remains a central obstacle to continual learning in LLMs. Recent works connect forgetting to how far, and along which directions, fine-tuning moves the weights. On-policy methods such as reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation avoid updating the principal singular directions of weight matrices and thus forget less. In contrast, SFT concentrates updates along these directions and is susceptible to catastrophic forgetting. In this work, we introduce Subspace Tuning (SST), which restricts each weight update to the bottom singular subspace, eliminating changes along the principal directions. SST is optimizer-agnostic and composes well with fine-tuning recipes including SFT and self-distillation. SST combines tight subspace protection, dense gradient estimation, and a simple refresh mechanism, enabling stronger learning than prior orthogonal fine-tuning methods. With these mechanisms, protecting as much as 99\% of the weight subspace substantially improves retention while preserving strong target-task performance. This behavior strengthens with model and data size and nearly eliminates forgetting in the large-model regime. SST also keeps the model close to its base distribution, inducing $2$--$4\times$ less KL drift than the baseline recipes. Overall, SST advances the learning--forgetting Pareto frontier, making it a practical default for fine-tuning pre-trained language models.

items.title_en: CAT-alyzing Honesty: Continuous Adversarial Training for Transferable LLM Honesty
items.title_zh: CAT催化诚实：面向可迁移LLM诚实性的连续对抗训练
items.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming prevalent in scenarios where honesty is critical. However, despite alignment training, these models still exhibit dishonest behaviour, such as outputting claims that contradict some knowledge or are not supported by what is accessible in context. We introduce Continuous Adversarial Training for Consistent Honesty (CATCH), inspired by a method originally developed to robustly refuse harmful queries. CATCH trains the model towards an honest answer and away from a dishonest one while maintaining the model's capabilities. We evaluate two architectures (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and Qwen3-3.6-27B). We show that trained with only hundreds of targets built from self-reporting scenarios, CATCH learns an honest behaviour that robustly generalizes and transfers across distinct benchmarks. It consistently reduces dishonesty under pressure on MASK, increases confessions in the multi-agent game of Among Us, and improves the discovery rates of the model's hidden behaviours in AuditBench. We show that CATCH outperforms prompting and supervised fine-tuning in improving honesty, and it is on par with state-of-the-art honesty activation steering. However, CATCH surpasses honesty steering in maintaining utility, thanks to a novel choice of utility data.

items.title_en: Learning Rational Strategies for Temporal Objectives in Multi-Agent Systems
items.title_zh: 多智能体系统中时序目标的理性策略学习
items.abstract_en: We study rational synthesis for stochastic multi-agent systems with unknown dynamics, where each agent is equipped with its own probabilistic temporal objective specified using Probabilistic Linear Temporal Logic on Finite Traces ($\mathsf{PLTL}_f}$). We impose solution concepts (e.g., Nash equilibrium, subgame-perfect equilibrium) as constraints on the joint strategy profile, using payoffs derived from each agent's probability of satisfying its temporal objective. In particular, we formulate per-agent rational synthesis as finding a strategy profile -- if one exists -- such that (i) the designated agent's probabilistic temporal constraint is satisfied, and (ii) the profile represents a stable solution under a chosen solution concept. We give conditional convergence guarantees for tabular Nash-Q learning, certify satisfaction with simultaneous finite-sample confidence bounds, and assess strategic stability with approximate best-response checking. Our approach operates in a stochastic \emph{Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning} (MARL) environment, where model-free learning algorithms attempt to attain extremal satisfaction probabilities for temporal objectives automatically compiled into reward automata. Our approach is empirically validated using 8 general-sum concurrent stochastic games.

items.title_en: Asking Smarter Questions: Targeted Active Preference Learning for Underspecified Rewards
items.title_zh: 提出更聪明的问题：面向欠指定奖励的针对性主动偏好学习
items.abstract_en: Reward learning typically assumes the human's input covers everything that matters for the task. In practice, humans can only attend to so much at once, so their teaching naturally captures some features---or aspects of the task---better than others. Prior work has shown how the robot can identify which features were poorly supervised directly from its teaching data. But the current solution is to ask the human to try again, putting the burden on someone who already struggled to convey those features. We propose shifting this burden to the robot. Our key insight is that the same information that tells the robot what it doesn't know can help it ask better questions. Preference queries offer a low-effort channel for resolving this uncertainty, but only if the robot knows where to direct them and the human knows what to attend to when answering. We act on this insight in two ways: we build an informed prior that targets preference queries at the features that need resolving, and we accompany each query with an explanation that focuses the human's attention on exactly those features. In simulation, the informed prior beats the standard active preference learning baseline by up to $30.8\%$ in the low-query regime, where reducing human effort matters most. In a user study, the informed prior and explanations each significantly improve reward recovery and amplify each other.

items.title_en: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
items.title_zh: 图书管理员智能体：训练LLM整理能预测未来查询的长上下文工作区
items.abstract_en: Reasoning over long document contexts remains a challenge for large language models (LLMs). Standard retrieval methods are inherently reactive, bottlenecking agents with complex, cross-document reasoning at inference time, while precomputed structures like knowledge graphs often fall short because they rely on rigid heuristics. Instead, can we allow agents to perform anticipatory directed curation: learning to proactively reorganize unstructured corpora prior to inference to efficiently serve diverse future queries. We build on a key asymmetry in modern agentic harnesses (e.g., Claude Code): while LLM agents are adept at navigating existing filesystems to solve an immediate task, they are rarely trained to construct reusable workspaces for future use. To instantiate this capability, we introduce Librarian Agents, a framework in which a builder agent transforms raw documents into a hierarchical filesystem of synthetic files and reference links, which forms a workspace tailored for a downstream answering agent. We formulate workspace construction as a Markov decision process and optimize the builder policy via reinforcement learning to directly maximize downstream answering accuracy. Empirically, Librarian Agents outperforms the strongest retrieval and precomputation baselines by 33 percentage points on BrowseComp-Plus, amortizes upfront construction costs across repeated queries, and generalizes zero-shot to unseen domains on BRIGHT with a 31-point average accuracy improvement.

items.title_en: X-RIC: An Agentic RAN-Intelligent Controller Benchmark for Enhancing Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: X-RIC：一个增强强化学习的智能体式RAN智能控制器基准
items.abstract_en: The O-RAN ALLIANCE introduces architectural flexibility through disaggregation and AI-driven control. While the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) enables centralized optimization, current AI approaches lack reasoning capabilities and explainability. We propose eXplainable RIC (X-RIC), a novel framework integrating agentic AI into O-RAN architectures. X-RIC combines reactive Reinforcement Learning (RL) with strategic agentic reasoning through: (i) automated Behavioral Cloning (BC) using domain heuristics for sample-efficient training, (ii) a Telecom Language Model (TLM), a transformer-based reasoning module providing contextual abstraction and interpretability, and (iii) closed-loop co-adaptation within the Near-RT RIC control loop enabling continuous policy refinement. To ensure deployment readiness, we introduce BARX (Benchmarking Agentic Reasoning for RAN), a domain-specific evaluation framework assessing agentic control across latency, compliance, and determinism metrics. We validate X-RIC on SLA-aware network slicing in simulation and O-RAN-compliant testbed deployments. X-RIC achieves 89% operational cost reduction while maintaining SLA compliance, converging 75% faster with 50% fewer training steps and 46% lower variance.

items.title_en: Baselines and Score Centering in Policy Gradient Estimation
items.title_zh: 策略梯度估计中的基线与分数中心化
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning has become a widely used approach to post-training large language models. In a typical implementation, learning is off-policy: The policy generating the responses differs from the policy being trained because of training-inference mismatch or policy staleness in asynchronous training. This discrepancy is commonly addressed by importance sampling, whose ratio is usually regularized in practice through truncation, masking, or clipping. Under regularized importance sampling, the importance-weighted policy gradient is no longer invariant to constant shifts in the reward. This invariance is recovered by using the covariance between the reward and the importance-weighted score as the estimand, which coincides with the policy gradient when the ratio is not regularized. This note develops this covariance perspective for both sequence-level and token-level importance sampling. The covariance perspective reveals the roles of the group-mean baseline and score centering in policy gradient estimation. Both perform centering in covariance estimation, but they differ in the mean being subtracted: The group-mean baseline uses a sample mean, whereas score centering uses a population mean. The two lead to distinct unbiased covariance estimators with different variances. Whether both forms of centering should be used simultaneously depends on whether importance sampling is applied at the sequence level or at the token level. With sequence-level importance sampling, score centering adds no benefit once the group-mean baseline is used; with token-level importance sampling, using the group-mean baseline without score centering generally introduces bias when the importance ratio is regularized.

items.title_en: Topology-Inspired Fine-Tuning for Wind-Field Super-Resolution
items.title_zh: 面向风场超分辨率的拓扑启发式微调
items.abstract_en: Scientific super-resolution (SR) models are typically optimized with pointwise reconstruction losses, yet scientific interpretation often hinges on extrema, connected regions, and multiscale scalar structure. We characterize this tension with pretrained CNN and GAN wind-field SR models. Pointwise metrics, bottleneck persistence-diagram (PD) distance, and merge-tree (MT) distance favor the CNN, whereas order-2 Wasserstein PD distances favor the sharper GAN, so even different distances on the same topological descriptor reward different properties. Motivated by this disagreement, we fine-tune the pretrained CNN with differentiable topology-inspired auxiliary losses on scalar speed, gradient magnitude, soft high-speed level sets, and local maxima, and with fixed-pair supervision, which constrains predicted values and persistence at ground-truth persistence-pair endpoints located offline with the Topology ToolKit. A loss study of 16 fine-tuning configurations, each compared with a matched standard fine-tuning control that uses only the original reconstruction loss, on a fixed 168-field benchmark (with topology evaluated on a fixed 160 by 160 subregion of each field), shows that, among the scalar-field losses, gradient supervision provides the strongest PD improvement but does not improve mean MT distance, whereas fixed-pair supervision gives the largest and most consistent joint improvement in PD and MT distances. The final objective combines these two signals. Relative to the pretrained CNN, it lowers mean bottleneck, $W_{2,\infty}$, and $W_{2,2}$ distances by 31%, 25%, and 27% (and by 32-35% relative to the control, which on its own worsens all three), lowers all three on 150 of 168 fields, and gains 1.30 dB PSNR, about half the gain of standard fine-tuning. Mean MT distance also improves, but on only 91 of those 150 fields, indicating that PD and MT capture complementary structure.

items.title_en: BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks
items.abstract_en: Reducing memory use in large language model (LLM) training is an ongoing challenge. Activation checkpointing saves memory by recomputation, while lossy compression changes the stored activations. The reemergence of sparse $\relu$ and $\relu^2$ activations creates a third opportunity: losslessly compressing the activation cache itself. We present BitSparse, a GPU-resident lossless compression format for sparse activations. Compression and reconstruction run in custom Triton kernels fused into an autograd function, shrinking the activation cache while recovering it exactly for the backward pass. Bfloat16 (BF16) and FP8 activations are supported. Optional sign-bit packing further increases compression up to close to the theoretical limit. We analyze its compression ratio and compare it to the theoretical optimum. BitSparse lowers per-token VRAM by 31\% and 30\% Modded-NanoGPT and Nemotron-H respectively, with overheads of no more than 1\% at practical sequence lengths. Additionally, a new preallocated buffer system avoids host synchronization during training when variable size tensors are allocated.

items.title_en: Explore Once, Evaluate Many: Multiple Policy Evaluation for Stochastic Linear Bandits
items.abstract_en: We study how to evaluate $K$ target policies simultaneously in stochastic contextual bandits with linear reward structure. Given a known $d$-dimensional feature map and reward-free access to policy queries, we propose PRISMA (Policy evaluation through Regularized Information Sharing and Mixture Allocation), an algorithm that estimates every target policy's value to accuracy $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-δ$. The algorithm uses $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left( \frac{(L^2S^2+β^2)(1\veeρ^\star)}{\varepsilon^2} \cdot \log(K) \right)$ context draws and reward observations, where $ρ^\star\le d$ is an instance-dependent measure of the difficulty of designing a shared sampling distribution. Here, $L$, $S$, and $β$ bound the feature norm, reward parameter norm, and reward noise, respectively, and the suppressed factors are logarithmic in $K$, $d$, and $1/δ$. Our method combines reward-free planning, a regularized sampling design, and a single ridge regression estimator shared across all target policies. An adaptive doubling procedure selects the regularization scale without knowledge of $ρ^\star$. The guarantees require no numerical lower bound on second-moment eigenvalues and have no explicit dependence on the cardinalities of the context and action spaces. Policy-query costs are accounted for separately, with $K$ queries per shared planning context.
